text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET STORIES
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- Illegal imports of Russian made CFC 12 gas used in production of refrigeration equipment account for over 30 percent of its sales in Poland, the ozone layer protection office said.
Poland stopped production and imports of the gas last year but domestic demand has remained high.
- The Anco firm of Gdansk will shortly launch Europe's first software for the internet telephone module.
Prior to Anco similar software applications were introduced by U.S. and Israeli firms.

- State-owned PKO BP bank and Bank Rozwoju Eksportu (BRE) have enhanced their market position while that of Bank Handlowy and Pekao SA has decreased, a bank rating by the Gdansk-based market research economy institute said.
- Around 47 percent of Poles buy Danone yogurt and 17 percent buy Laciate milk, the country's favourite choice in these product lines, a survey by the PBS polling institute said.
- Poland's market has room for three or four big foundry groups each boasting annual output capacity of 100,000 tonnes, Odlewnie Polskie foundry holding head Boguslaw Peczela said.
- Over 30 percent of Poles use no financial instruments whatsoever but the number of people who declare no savings is declining, a survey by the PBS polling agency said.

- The MZPOW fruit and vegetable processing group in central Poland has invested 20 million zlotys for the modernisation and construction of new production lines in the last four years, the company said.

- The First Polish American Bank (PPABank) invested $1.6 million in computer-systems development in the last two years, allowing it to offer a cash management system to customers while not leaving their offices, the bank said.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI
- The MacroSoft software firm lists its stock on the CTO regulated over-the-counter market on Monday.
- Poland's trade with African countries accounted for 1.32 percent of the total foreign trade exchange in 1996, showing a slight decline compared with the year before, the economy ministry said.
- The TFP Skarbiec investment trust will launch investment units in the next two months, trust president Zenon Slomski said.
- The Aqua civil engineering firm in Bielsko-Biala plans to apply for a listing on the regulated over-the-counter (OTC) market, Aqua's president Bogdan Traczyk said.
Aqua's net profit in the first six months of 1997 was 1.89 million zlotys.
- The Nowy Sacz provincial branch of Bank Gospodarki Zywnosciowej (BGZ) agricultural sector bank has launched preferential credits for flood victims.
Recent floods brought the province losses of 300 million zlotys.
GAZETA WYBORCZA

- Poland's biggest private footwear maker But-s in Konstantynow Lodzki, central Poland, plans a share listing on the Warsaw bourse's parallel market by the second half of 1998, company president Zbigniew Smyczek said.
ZYCIE
- Bank Gospodarki Zywnosciowej's (BGZ) gross profit reached 317.3 million zlotys in the first half of 1997, showing 35 percent growth compared with the same period last year, the bank said.
NOTE - Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
